questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

1. If the Legislative Assembly of a State in India is dissolved in mid-term, the Speaker vacates his office.

2. When the Speaker of a Legislative Assembly resigns, he addresses his letter to the Governor of the State.

Which of the statements given above is/ are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither 1 nor 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Speaker in Legislative Assembly**:

 
• **Article 178 **of the constitution provides for offices of the **Speaker and Deputy Speake**r in the** state legislature**.
 
• The Speaker is elected by the assembly itself from amongst its members.
 
• Usually, the **Speaker** remains in office during the **life of the assembly.**
 
• However, he vacates his office earlier in any of the following three cases:
 
 
• if he ceases to be a member of the assembly
 
• if he resigns by writing to the **deputy speaker**. **Hence statement 2 is incorrect. **
 
• if he is **removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members **of the assembly. Such a resolution can be moved only after giving **14 days** advance notice.
 
 
 
• Speaker has the following **powers and duties**:
 
 
• He** maintains order and decorum in the assembly f**or conducting its business and regulating its proceedings. This is his primary responsibility and he has** final powe**r in this regard.
 
• He is the **final interpreter** of the provisions of (a) **the Constitution of India, (b) the rules of procedure and conduct of the business of the assembly, and (c) the legislative precedents, within the assembly.**
 
• He adjourns the assembly or suspends the meeting in the **absence of a quorum**.
 
• He does not vote in the first instance. But, he can **exercise a casting vote in the case of a tie**.
 
• He can allow **a ‘secret’ sitting of the House **at the request of the leader of the House.
 
• He decides whether a bill is **a Money Bill or not** and his decision on this question is** final.**
 
• He decides the questions of** disqualification of a membe**r of the assembly, arising on the ground of defection under the provisions of the **Tenth Schedule.**
 
• He appoints the **chairman of all the committees **of the assembly and supervises their functioning. He himself is the chairman of the **Business Advisory Committee, the Rules Committee and the General Purpose Committee.**
 
 
 
• Under** Article 179** of the constitution, whenever the** Assembly is dissolved**, the **Speaker shall not vacate his office **until immediately **before the first meeting of the Assembly after the Dissolution. *Hence Statement 1 is incorrect. ***

questions.question: What does ‘Chaitya’ in Buddhist architecture refer to?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Prayer hall__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Buddhist Architecture is primarily represented by three prominent building types:

 
 
• The Chaitya Hall (Place Of Worship or Prayer hall)
 
• The Vihara (Monastery)
 
• The Stupa (Hemispherical Mound For Worship/Memory)
 
 
 
• Chaitya is a place of worship, while Vihara is the dwelling place of the monks.
 
• Both early Chaityas and Viharas were made from woods and later stone-cut Chaityas and Viharas were made.
 
• Chaitya was a rectangular prayer hall with a stupa placed in the centre, the purpose was prayer.
 
• The Chaitya was divided into three parts and had an apsidal ending, that is, a semicircular rear end.
 
• The central part of the hall (also called the nave) was separated from the two aisles by two rows of pillars.
 
• The chaityas also had polished interior walls, semicircular roofs and horse-shoe-shaped windows called the Chaitya windows.
 
• Viharas were the residences of the monks.
 
• ​Distinctive Buddhist architectural structures and sculptures like Stupas, Pagodas, caves, and monasteries
 
• Being the spiritual symbols of Buddhism, these structures are monastic or holy places
 
• They also serve as a sacred land that has the power to purify one’s soul.

questions.question: In which of the following inscriptions of Ashoka his name 'Ashoka' has been mentioned?
questions.solution:
In the __**Maski Inscription**__ of Ashoka his name 'Ashoka' has been mentioned.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• In the Maski Inscription, the name **"Ashoka"** is mentioned.
 
• The Maski Inscription is one of the earliest known inscriptions of Ashoka, discovered in Maski, Karnataka, India.
 
• It is a rock edict written in the Brahmi script and Prakrit language.
 
• The Maski Inscription refers to the emperor as **"Devanampriya Ashoka"** or** "Beloved of the Gods Ashoka."**
 
• This inscription, along with others, provides insights into Ashoka's policies, his **conversion to Buddhism**, and his efforts to promote Dhamma (righteousness) throughout his empire.
 
• 
 
The Maski Inscription serves as an important historical and archaeological artefact that helps us understand the reign and legacy of Ashoka the Great.

 

So the correct answer is **Maski Inscription.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Bhabra Rock Edict and Ahraura Inscription were another rock edict of Ashoka, but it does not mention his name. Instead, it refers to the ruler as "Devanampriya" or "Beloved of the Gods".
 
• The Nettur Inscription and the Rupnath Inscription are both minor rock edicts of Ashoka, and they do not mention his name either.

questions.question: Which institute’s researchers have developed a nanotechnology-based biosensor capable of detecting Parkinson’s Disease before symptoms appear?

options.text: National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences (NIMHANS), Bengaluru

The correct answer is __**Institute of Nano Science and Technology (INST), Mohali.**__

__

__
 
• **The biosensor uses gold nanoclusters (AuNCs), ultrasmall glowing particles only a few nanometres wide.**
 
• **Proline-coated clusters bind to normal α-synuclein protein, which is harmless.**
 
• **Histidine-coated clusters bind to aggregated amyloid α-synuclein, which causes Parkinson’s disease.**
 
• **This allows the sensor to distinguish between healthy and harmful protein states, enabling early diagnosis of Parkinson’s.**

• Caused by the loss of dopamine-producing neurons in the brain.
 
• Linked to abnormal misfolding and aggregation of α-synuclein protein.
 
• Symptoms include tremors, rigidity, slowness of movement, and postural instability.
 
 
 
• Gold Nanoclusters (AuNCs)__
 __
 
• Ultrasmall nanoparticles with glowing properties, only a few nanometres wide.
 
• Modified with amino acids for selective binding to proteins.
 
 
 
• Significance__

Consider the following statements regarding the President of India:

1. In the case of the pregnancy of a woman offender, he may completely absolve her guilt using Respite power.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 only.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Judicial Powers of the President of India:**

 
 
• The President appoints the Chief Justice & other Judges of the S.C & H.C.
 
• Under Article 143, he can seek advice from S.C on any question of law.
 
 
• The advice tendered by S.C is not binding on the President.
 
 
 
• Article 72 confers the President power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment or to commute the sentence of any person convicted of an offence.
 
 
• **Pardoning powers of the President include**:
 
 
• **Pardon:** Completely absolves the guilt of the offender.
 
• **Reprieve:** It refers to the temporary stay on the death sentence or life imprisonment.
 
• **Respite:** It refers to the awarding a lesser sentence on a special ground like the pregnancy of a woman offender.
 
 
• **Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.**
 
 
 
• **Remission:** Reducing the amount of sentence without changing the nature of punishment.
 
• **Commutation: **Changing one punishment to another form from a death sentence to life imprisonment.

• The petitioner has no right to an oral hearing by the President.
 
• The President can examine the evidence afresh taking a view different from the courts.
 
• President exercises this power on the advice of the Union Cabinet.
 
 
 
• The President while using this power, does not act as a court of appeal.
 
 
• **Hence, statement 2 is correct.**

questions.question: A collection of programs that controls how the computer system runs and processes information is called

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operating System**

 
 
• **It collection of programs that controls how the computer system runs and processes information**__.
 
• It consists of programs, which controls, coordinate and supervise the activities of the various components of a computer system.
 
• Its function is to provide a link between the computer hardware and the user.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• A **compiler** is a software tool that converts the source code written in a high-level programming language like C++, Java, or Python into machine code or executable code that can be run on a computer.
 
• An **assembler **is a software tool that converts assembly language code into machine code. 
 
 
• Assembly language is a low-level programming language that is closer to machine language than high-level languages. 
 
• An assembler translates assembly code instructions into machine code instructions that can be executed by a computer.
 
 
 
• A **linker **is a software tool that combines object files and libraries to create an executable file or a shared library. 
 
 
• When a program is compiled, it is usually split into multiple object files, each containing a portion of the program's code. 
 
• The linker takes these object files and combines them to create an executable file or a shared library that can be run on a computer.

questions.question: Which of the following philosophies claimed that Vasna and Trishna lie at the root of human suffering?
questions.solution:
Buddhist philosophy and doctrines, based on the teachings of Gautama Buddha, give meaningful insights about reality and human existence. Buddha was primarily an ethical teacher rather than a philosopher.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Buddha's central concern was to show man the way out of suffering and not one of constructing a philosophical theory. Therefore, Buddha’s teaching lays great emphasis on the practical matters of conduct which lead to liberation.

Buddhism philosophy claimed that Vasna and Trishna lie at the root of human suffering as the four noble truths of Buddhism are as follows:

 
• Life is Full of Suffering (Dukkha): According to the first noble truth, all forms of existence are subject to suffering. Buddhism recognizes suffering at three levels, such as:

 
 
• the suffering we experience in our daily life, like, birth, sickness, old age, death, despair, pain, desire, etc.
 
• the suffering caused by the internal mental conditions and the activities of the sense organs.
 
 
 
• Suffering has a Cause (Dukkha samudaya): Everything in this cosmos has a cause, and nothing exists and happens without a cause. If this is the case, suffering should also have a cause and the roots of human suffering include:
 
 
• Vasna: A subtle form of desire, a hidden desire.
 
• Trishna: Intense craving or hankering after sensual objects.
 
 
 
• Cessation of Suffering (Dukkha nirodha): If suffering has a cause, the seeker has to destroy this cause to stop suffering. So desire has to be extinguished to stop suffering. Nirvana is the state of being without suffering. It is a state of supreme happiness and bliss.
 
• Ways to Destroy Suffering (Dukkha-nirodha-marga): The ways to destroy suffering consists of the practice of the eightfold virtue, such as Right View, Right Aspiration, Right Speech, Right Conduct, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Awareness, and Right Concentration.

Hence, it could be concluded that Buddhism philosophy claimed that Vasna and Trishna lie at the root of human suffering. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **Hint__**

 
 

 Vedanta Philosophy
 Vedanta, an idealistic philosophy, admits the objective reality of the world for all practical purposes. Moksa is the ultimate goal of life. It is the liberation from all worldly bondage. 
 
 

 Jainism Philosophy

questions.question: If x⁴+(1)/(x⁴)=194, x>0 , then find the value of x³+(1)/(x³)+x+(1)/(x).

If x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = k, then x² + 1/x² = √(k + 2) and x + 1/x = √(√(k + 2) + 2)

⇒ x + 1/x = √(√(194 + 2) + 2) = √(14 + 2) = √16 = 4

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ = 4³ − 3 × 4 = 52

⇒ Required expression = (x³ + 1/x³) + (x + 1/x) = 52 + 4 = 56

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = 194, where x > 0

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

a³ + b³ = (a + b)³ − 3ab(a + b)

**Calculations:**

⇒ x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = 194

⇒ x⁴ + 1/x⁴ + 2 = 194 + 2

⇒ (x² + 1/x²)² = 196

⇒ x² + 1/x² = 14 (since x > 0)

⇒ x² + 1/x² + 2 = 14 + 2

⇒ (x + 1/x)² = 16

⇒ x + 1/x = 4

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ = (x + 1/x)³ − 3(x + 1/x)

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ = 4³ − 3 × 4

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ = 64 − 12 = 52

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ + x + 1/x = 52 + 4 = 56

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Shortcuts for Cubes

Higher Powers Extraction

questions.question: The value of 1³-8²+((36)/(4))²-0+2times 5= ______
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Directly apply BODMAS to solve the given expression.

⇒ 1³ − 8² + (36 ÷ 4)² − 0 + 2 × 5

⇒ 1 − 64 + 9² + 10

⇒ 1 − 64 + 81 + 10 = 92 − 64 = 28

**∴ The correct answer is 28.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: 1³ − 8² + (36 ÷ 4)² − 0 + 2 × 5

**Formula Used:**

BODMAS Rule (Bracket, Order, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1³ − 8² + (36 ÷ 4)² − 0 + 2 × 5

Solving the Bracket first:

⇒ 36 ÷ 4 = 9

⇒ The expression becomes: 1³ − 8² + 9² − 0 + 2 × 5

Solving Orders (exponents):

⇒ 1³ = 1

⇒ 8² = 64

⇒ 9² = 81

⇒ The expression becomes: 1 − 64 + 81 − 0 + 2 × 5

Solving Multiplication:

⇒ 2 × 5 = 10

⇒ The expression becomes: 1 − 64 + 81 − 0 + 10

Solving Addition and Subtraction from left to right:

⇒ (1 + 81 + 10) − 64 − 0

⇒ 92 − 64

⇒ 28

**∴ The correct answer is 28.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It dictates the precise sequence for evaluating a mathematical expression: Bracket, Order (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Rules of Exponents

Any non-zero number a raised to the power 0 is 1 (a⁰ = 1). In addition, the number 1 raised to any power will always result in 1.

Fraction Simplification

Always simplify fractional divisions inside brackets completely before calculating any external powers, as it prevents working with unnecessarily large numbers.

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio of 5 ∶ 13. If their HCF is 11, find the numbers respectively?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If two numbers are in the simplified ratio a : b, the actual numbers are obtained directly by multiplying with their HCF.

Given the ratio = 5 : 13 and HCF = 11.

First number = 5 × 11 = 55

Second number = 13 × 11 = 143

**∴ The correct answer is 55 and 143.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The ratio of the two numbers = 5 : 13

Highest Common Factor (HCF) = 11

**Concept Used:**

When two numbers are expressed as a simplified ratio, they are mutually prime (co-prime), and their highest common multiplying factor is their HCF.

 First Number (Ratio = 5)
 
 5 units
 × HCF (11) → 55
 Second Number (Ratio = 13)
 
 13 units
 × HCF (11) → 143

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the two numbers be 5x and 13x.

⇒ Since 5 and 13 have no common factor other than 1, the highest common factor of 5x and 13x is exactly x.

⇒ We are given that the HCF is 11, therefore x = 11.

⇒ First number = 5x = 5 × 11 = 55

⇒ Second number = 13x = 13 × 11 = 143

**∴ The correct answer is 55 and 143.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM of Ratio-based Numbers

If two numbers are in ratio a : b with a common HCF equal to H, their least common multiple is calculated directly by LCM = H × a × b.

Product of Two Numbers

The product of any two numbers is mathematically always equal to the product of their HCF and LCM (First Number × Second Number = HCF × LCM).

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their HCF is strictly 1. The numerical parts of any completely reduced ratio are inherently co-prime.
</p

questions.question: ( {{{tan }²}theta + {{cot }²}theta + 2} ) div ( {(1)/({1 + cos theta )} + (1)/({1 - cos theta )}} ), 0° < θ < 90°, is equal to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Put θ = 60° in the given expression.

Left part = tan²60° + cot²60° + 2 = (√3)² + (1/√3)² + 2 = 3 + 1/3 + 2 = 16/3

Right part = 1 / (1 + cos60°) + 1 / (1 − cos60°) = 1 / (1 + 1/2) + 1 / (1 − 1/2) = 2/3 + 2 = 8/3

Expression value = (16/3) ÷ (8/3) = 2

Checking Option 3: sec²60° / 2 = (2)² / 2 = 4 / 2 = 2 (matches exactly).

**∴ The correct answer is sec²θ / 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(tan²θ + cot²θ + 2) ÷ [1 / (1 + cosθ) + 1 / (1 − cosθ)]

**Formula Used:**

tan²θ + 1 = sec²θ | cot²θ + 1 = cosec²θ | 1 − cos²θ = sin²θ

**Calculations:**

⇒ First part = tan²θ + cot²θ + 2

⇒ First part = (tan²θ + 1) + (cot²θ + 1) = sec²θ + cosec²θ

⇒ First part = 1 / cos²θ + 1 / sin²θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ) / (sin²θ × cos²θ)

⇒ First part = 1 / (sin²θ × cos²θ) = sec²θ × cosec²θ

⇒ Second part = 1 / (1 + cosθ) + 1 / (1 − cosθ)

⇒ Second part = [(1 − cosθ) + (1 + cosθ)] / [(1 + cosθ) × (1 − cosθ)]

⇒ Second part = 2 / (1 − cos²θ) = 2 / sin²θ = 2cosec²θ

⇒ Substituting both parts back into the given expression:

⇒ Expression = (sec²θ × cosec²θ) ÷ 2cosec²θ

⇒ Expression = sec²θ / 2

**∴ The correct answer is sec²θ / 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Trigonometric Identities

The three fundamental identities are: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.

Sum to Product Transformation

A very useful simplification trick for competitive exams: sec²θ + cosec²θ = sec²θ × cosec²θ.

Reciprocal Functions

Remember that cosecθ = 1 / sinθ, secθ = 1 / cosθ, and cotθ = cosθ / sinθ.
</p

questions.question: A table and a swing were sold for Rs. 9,936 each. The table was sold for a profit of 8% and the swing was sold for a loss of 8%. What is the gain or loss percentage in the whole transaction?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When two articles are sold at the exact same selling price, one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%, the entire transaction always results in an overall loss.

Overall Loss % = (x² ÷ 100)%

⇒ Overall Loss % = (8² ÷ 100)% = (64 ÷ 100)% = 0.64%

**∴ The correct answer is 0.64% loss.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) of the table = ₹9936

Selling Price (SP) of the swing = ₹9936

Profit on the table = 8%

Loss on the swing = 8%

 
 CP1 = 9200
 
 

 Profit = +8% (+736)

 
 SP1 = 9936

 
 CP2 = 10800
 
 

 Loss = −8% (−864)

 
 SP2 = 9936
 
 Total CP = 20000 | Total SP = 19872 | Loss = 128
 Overall Loss % = (128 ÷ 20000) × 100 = 0.64%

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Selling Price = 9936 + 9936 = ₹19872

⇒ Cost Price of the table (CP₁) = SP × [100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)]

⇒ CP₁ = 9936 × (100 ÷ 108) = 9936 × (25 ÷ 27) = ₹9200

⇒ Cost Price of the swing (CP₂) = SP × [100 ÷ (100 − Loss%)]

⇒ CP₂ = 9936 × (100 ÷ 92) = 9936 × (25 ÷ 23) = ₹10800

⇒ Total Cost Price = 9200 + 10800 = ₹20000

⇒ Total Loss = Total CP − Total SP = 20000 − 19872 = ₹128

⇒ Overall Loss % = (Total Loss ÷ Total CP) × 100

⇒ Overall Loss % = (128 ÷ 20000) × 100 = 0.64%

**∴ The correct answer is 0.64% loss.**

**__Additional Information__**

Same SP, Same Profit & Loss %

When two items are sold at the same selling price, one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%, there is always a net loss. The loss percentage is consistently determined using the formula (x² ÷ 100)%.

Same CP, Same Profit & Loss %

When two items are bought at the identical cost price, and one is sold at a profit of x% while the other at a loss of x%, the net result is zero, meaning there is no net profit and no net loss overall.

Marked Price and CP Relation

The direct ratio comparing Marked Price (MP) and Cost Price (CP) when dealing with profit and discount is written directly as: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).
</p

questions.question: Find the remainder when 212×213×214 is divided by 6.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The product of any 'n' consecutive integers is always exactly divisible by n!.

Here, 212, 213, and 214 are 3 consecutive integers.

So, their product is exactly divisible by 3! = 3 × 2 × 1 = 6.

Since the product is perfectly divisible by 6, it leaves no remainder.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = 212 × 213 × 214

Divisor = 6

**Concept Used:**

The remainder of a product of numbers is equal to the product of their individual remainders divided by the divisor.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Remainder when 212 is divided by 6 = 2 (since 210 is a multiple of 6)

⇒ Remainder when 213 is divided by 6 = 3 (since 210 is a multiple of 6)

⇒ Remainder when 214 is divided by 6 = 4 (since 210 is a multiple of 6)

⇒ Product of individual remainders = 2 × 3 × 4 = 24

⇒ Final remainder = Remainder when 24 is divided by 6

⇒ Since 24 is a multiple of 6, it is perfectly divisible by 6.

⇒ Therefore, the remainder is 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility of Consecutive Integers

The product of 'n' consecutive integers is always exactly divisible by n factorial (n!). For example, the product of 4 consecutive integers is always perfectly divisible by 4! = 24.

Remainder Theorem for Multiplication

If two numbers A and B have remainders r₁ and r₂ respectively when divided by a number N, then the remainder of (A × B) ÷ N is the exact same as the remainder of (r₁ × r₂) ÷ N.

Modular Arithmetic Rule

(A × B × C) mod N = [(A mod N) × (B mod N) × (C mod N)] mod N. This fundamental property simplifies complex multiplication problems by reducing numbers before multiplying.
</p

questions.question: Zeroes of a cubic polynomial p(x) are 3, −6, and 7. The coefficient of 'x' in p(x) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a polynomial p(x) with leading coefficient 1, the coefficient of 'x' is the sum of the product of the zeroes taken two at a time.

Let the zeroes be α = 3, β = −6, γ = 7

⇒ Coefficient of x = (α × β) + (β × γ) + (γ × α)

⇒ Coefficient of x = (3 × −6) + (−6 × 7) + (7 × 3)

⇒ Coefficient of x = −18 − 42 + 21 = −39

**∴ The correct answer is −39.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Zeroes of a cubic polynomial are 3, −6, and 7.

**Formula Used:**

A cubic polynomial p(x) with zeroes α, β, and γ is represented as:

p(x) = (x − α)(x − β)(x − γ)

**Calculation:**

⇒ p(x) = (x − 3)(x − (−6))(x − 7)

⇒ p(x) = (x − 3)(x + 6)(x − 7)

First, expanding (x − 3) and (x + 6):

⇒ p(x) = (x² + 6x − 3x − 18)(x − 7)

⇒ p(x) = (x² + 3x − 18)(x − 7)

Next, multiplying the resulting quadratic with (x − 7):

⇒ p(x) = x(x² + 3x − 18) − 7(x² + 3x − 18)

⇒ p(x) = (x³ + 3x² − 18x) − (7x² + 21x − 126)

⇒ p(x) = x³ − 4x² − 39x + 126

Comparing this with the standard polynomial form, the coefficient of x is −39.

**∴ The correct answer is −39.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cubic Polynomial Standard Form

The standard representation of a cubic polynomial is ax³ + bx² + cx + d = 0.

Sum of Zeroes

The sum of the roots (α + β + γ) is equal to −b/a.

Sum of Product of Roots in Pairs

The value (αβ + βγ + γα) is equal to c/a, which directly gives the coefficient of x when the leading coefficient a = 1.

Product of Zeroes

The product of all zeroes (αβγ) is equal to −d/a.
</p

questions.question: Find the square of Z. Z is the remainder when the smallest 4-digit number is exactly divisible by 24 and 36 is divided by 40.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

LCM of 24 and 36 = 72.

Smallest 4-digit number is 1000, and the nearest multiple of 72 is 72 × 14 = 1008.

Z = Remainder when 1008 is divided by 40.

1008 = 40 × 25 + 8 ⇒ Z = 8.

Square of Z = 8² = 64.

**∴ The correct answer is 64.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Smallest 4-digit number exactly divisible by 24 and 36.

Z is the remainder when this number is divided by 40.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 24 = 2³ × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 36 = 2² × 3²

⇒ LCM of 24 and 36 = 2³ × 3² = 8 × 9 = 72

⇒ The smallest 4-digit number is 1000.

⇒ 1000 ÷ 72 = 13 with a remainder of 64.

⇒ To find the smallest 4-digit multiple of 72, add (72 − 64) to 1000.

⇒ Required 4-digit number = 1000 + 8 = 1008.

⇒ Now, divide 1008 by 40 to find Z.

⇒ 1008 = (40 × 25) + 8

⇒ Thus, remainder Z = 8.

⇒ We need to find the square of Z.

⇒ Z² = 8² = 64.

**∴ The correct answer is 64.**

**__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest positive integer that is perfectly divisible by each of the given numbers. It is found by multiplying the highest powers of all prime factors present in the numbers.

Finding a Number Divisible by N in a Range

To find the smallest multiple of a number N greater than a base number B, use the formula: B + (N − Remainder of B ÷ N).

Remainder Theorem (Basic Division)

For any integer division, Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder, where the Remainder is always strictly less than the Divisor.
</p

questions.question: Mohan ranks seventh from the top and twenty eighth from the bottom in a class. How many students are there in the class?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mohan ranks seventh from the top and twenty eighth from the bottom in a class.

**Concept Used:**

Total number of students = Rank from the top + Rank from the bottom - 1

**Calculation:**

Rank from the top = 7

Rank from the bottom = 28

Total number of students = Rank from the top + Rank from the bottom - 1

⇒ 7 + 28 - 1

⇒ 34

**∴ There are 34 students in the class.**
